root_cause_clusters.controller_compatibility: Inherited controller packaging and CLI capabilities do not match the project bootstrap/operator workflow.
root_cause_clusters.project_discovery: Project-local configuration and role discovery are not selected consistently from the operational working directory.
root_cause_clusters.data_and_secret_scope: Inventory precedence, nested variable contracts and encrypted secret boundaries are inconsistent across sites.
root_cause_clusters.orchestration_graph: Role invocation, dependency ordering and handler sequencing violate service prerequisites.
root_cause_clusters.syntax_and_schema: Several YAML/task constructs are structurally valid-looking but invalid to the Ansible parser or module argument schema.
root_cause_clusters.jinja_data_model: Templates assume the wrong shapes/types for cross-host, endpoint and policy data and mishandle absent/IPv6 values.

defects.observable_failure: Configuration bootstrap command exits because the inherited controller CLI does not expose the requested initialization action.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Hard-coding a config file can hide the first failure while leaving later controller/template compatibility failures active.

defects.observable_failure: A preflight expression accepted by the intended controller release is rejected or behaves differently under the inherited runtime.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Rewriting one expression for the old runtime leaves the intended project bootstrap contract unmet.

defects.observable_failure: Validation relies on modern result/templating semantics and produces misleading type behavior on the inherited controller.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Casting the single failing value does not restore consistent semantics across all renderers.

defects.observable_failure: Version/config diagnostics show a controller source and config location inconsistent with the project runbook.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Changing PATH alone can still leave the wrong config precedence or Python environment selected.

defects.observable_failure: Playbook execution cannot locate project roles when invoked from the documented project entrypoint.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Installing roles globally makes one machine pass while breaking project portability and grading isolation.

defects.observable_failure: The wrapper can be launched from a different working directory and silently selects a non-project Ansible configuration.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Running only from the repository root masks the portability requirement.

defects.observable_failure: One role name resolves to no project role even after the project role search root is available.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Renaming the directory without fixing the invocation/dependency contract can swap responsibilities downstream.

defects.observable_failure: A role-relative template/include reference resolves under one invocation style but not the documented orchestration path.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Using an absolute repository path makes the benchmark machine-specific.

defects.observable_failure: A site override unexpectedly replaces a structured application settings mapping, leaving nested keys undefined.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding the missing key at the point of failure duplicates configuration and obscures precedence.

defects.observable_failure: A host-level endpoint override has a different shape from the group contract and breaks later aggregation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Template-side defaults can make rendering succeed while producing the wrong backend topology.

defects.observable_failure: Sensitive service credentials are present as ordinary readable YAML instead of the encrypted-at-rest contract used by the project.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding no_log hides runtime output but does not protect committed data at rest.

defects.observable_failure: A vaulted variable is referenced outside the scope in which the encrypted vars file is loaded, yielding an undefined secret at render time.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Copying the decrypted value into another variable file defeats the secret boundary.

defects.observable_failure: Application configuration is rendered before identity/trust prerequisites have materialized their facts and files.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding retries hides dependency ordering and creates non-deterministic first-versus-second-run behavior.

defects.observable_failure: Proxy and telemetry responsibilities are invoked through swapped role identifiers, generating syntactically plausible but semantically wrong files.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing only one role label can cause both responsibilities to execute twice or not at all.

defects.observable_failure: A service reload handler can fire before the validated trust bundle has been atomically promoted.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Suppressing the handler makes the run green but leaves running services on stale trust material.

defects.observable_failure: A batch failure can still allow downstream validation/promotion tasks to execute for hosts whose prerequisites failed.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Global any_errors_fatal discards intended failure isolation across independent sites.

defects.observable_failure: A task block contains a misplaced task keyword that produces a parser-level conflicting action or invalid attribute error.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Deleting the keyword removes the symptom but can also remove the required privilege/conditional scope.

defects.observable_failure: A nested YAML sequence/mapping boundary causes module arguments to be parsed under the wrong task key.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Indenting until YAML parses can still leave the module schema semantically wrong.

defects.observable_failure: An assertion task mixes loop/control data at an invalid level and fails before checking fleet invariants.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Removing the loop validates only the first host and weakens the contract.

defects.observable_failure: A module parameter uses an obsolete or invalid argument shape, surfacing only after earlier parser failures are repaired.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Replacing the module with shell bypasses idempotency and semantic validation.

defects.observable_failure: Backend aggregation applies mapping/filter operations to mixed host data and fails when one host supplies a scalar-shaped override.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Skipping the bad host yields an incomplete production backend set.

defects.observable_failure: IPv6 endpoints are rendered without the required bracket normalization while IPv4 output remains apparently correct.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Wrapping every address in brackets corrupts IPv4 endpoint syntax.

defects.observable_failure: Cross-host hostvars aggregation dereferences a missing optional group/member before defaults are applied.
defects.partial_fix_trap: A broad default empty list hides required targets and makes monitoring silently incomplete.

defects.observable_failure: Policy rendering compares numeric/string values and composes defaults in an order that emits unstable or incorrect rule ordering.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Sorting the final text lexically creates a deterministic but semantically wrong priority order.

organic_f2p_surface_assessment: Twenty-four manifestations map to at least twenty-seven independent observable repair behaviors because several root causes affect separate bootstrap, render, promotion and idempotency surfaces. The graph has cross-cluster interactions so repairing parser errors alone or templating alone cannot pass the fleet contract.
